earnings.title: Veralto Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
highlights: Sales increased 7.5% year-over-year to $1,509 million, with non-GAAP core sales growth of 5.1%
Operating cash flow was $323 million and non-GAAP free cash flow was $304 million
Repurchased $550 million of shares, or 2.4% of outstanding shares (3)
(3) Year-to-date share repurchases as of October 28, 2026. 2.4% is calculated off the Company’s outstanding shares as of February 13, 2026

With annual sales of approximately $5.5 billion, Veralto is a global leader in essential technology solutions with a proven track record of solving some of the most complex challenges we face as a society.

quotes.text: We delivered outstanding third-quarter results, with broad-based sales growth and strong operating leverage across the portfolio. Total sales grew 7.5%, adjusted operating margin expanded 170 basis points and adjusted earnings per share increased 19.2% year over year.

outlook: For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company anticipates non-GAAP core sales growth in the range of 5.5% to 6.5% year-over-year.
Adjusted operating profit margin is expected to be approximately 24.5%, broadly in line with the prior year period, net of growth investments and the impact from acquisitions.
The Company’s fourth quarter adjusted diluted earnings per share guidance is in the range of $1.13 to $1.16 per share.
For the full year 2026, the Company raised its non-GAAP core sales growth to a range of 4.2% to 4.5% year-over-year, up from the prior guidance range of 4.0% to 4.5%.

items.heading: Conditions in the global economy, including military conflicts, the particular markets we serve and the financial markets can adversely affect our business and financial statements.

The U.S. government has imposed and may continue to impose significant tariffs or other restrictions on foreign imports, and such trade restrictions or related countermeasures taken by impacted foreign countries could negatively affect our business and financial statements.

We face intense competition and if we are unable to compete effectively, we may experience decreased demand and decreased market share. Even if we compete effectively, we may be required to reduce the prices we charge.
Our growth depends in part on the timely development and commercialization, and customer acceptance, of new and enhanced products and services based on technological innovation.
Uncertainties with respect to the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence in our business and products may result in harm to our business and financial statements.
Non-U.S. economic, political, legal, compliance, social and business factors can negatively affect our business and financial statements.
